## 1. Customer-value prediction (high-value = top 20% net spend in the next 90 days)

* **Selected model:** XGBoost
* **Selection rule:** highest validation PR-AUC among models with validation precision>=0.4 and recall>=0.5

* **Windows:** {"train": "2011-03-15 00:00:00", "val": "2011-06-13 00:00:00", "test": "2011-09-11 00:00:00", "end": "2011-12-10 00:00:00", "horizon_days": 90}
* **Sizes:** {"train": 4588, "val": 4952, "test": 5256}

### Best hyper-parameters (chosen on validation)

* **Logistic Regression**: `{"C": 0.01}`, decision threshold 0.288, 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training period 0.854 +/- 0.016
* **Random Forest**: `{"max_depth": 8, "min_samples_leaf": 3}`, decision threshold 0.247, 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training period 0.858 +/- 0.014
* **XGBoost**: `{"n_estimators": 150, "max_depth": 2, "learning_rate": 0.05}`, decision threshold 0.258, 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training period 0.859 +/- 0.015
* **RBF Network**: `{"n_centers": 50, "gamma": 0.03, "C": 10}`, decision threshold 0.275, 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training period 0.863 +/- 0.014
* **MLP Classifier**: `{"hidden_layer_sizes": [64, 32], "alpha": 0.01}`, decision threshold 0.372, 5-fold CV ROC-AUC on the training period 0.859 +/- 0.020

### Reading the results

* Differences between the models are small (see the table). For six-ish tabular features, model choice matters less than feature design and the time-split protocol.
* Precision/recall are reported at a threshold tuned on **validation**, then applied unchanged to test. The positive rate differs per window because the label is a per-window quantile.
* The test window is the Christmas quarter - a distribution shift versus the quieter training window. Test scores therefore measure robustness to seasonality, not only generalisation to new customers.


## 2. Recommenders (time-aware offline evaluation)

Fit on transactions before **2011-10-10**; evaluated on 800 customers against **new** products bought afterwards. Catalogue size at the split: 4,618. k = 5.

| model | precision@5 | recall@5 | ndcg@5 | coverage | avg_popularity_percentile | top10pct_item_share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| popularity | 0.0288 | 0.0086 | 0.0297 | 0.0093 | 0.9992 | 1.0000 |
| collaborative | 0.0618 | 0.0225 | 0.0654 | 0.0693 | 0.9819 | 0.9675 |
| content | 0.0595 | 0.0262 | 0.0686 | 0.1934 | 0.7510 | 0.3852 |
| hybrid | 0.0663 | 0.0275 | 0.0721 | 0.1061 | 0.9629 | 0.9080 |

Customers' actual new purchases sit at popularity percentile **0.71**; compare with the `avg_popularity_percentile` column to see which recommenders over-promote best-sellers.

Hybrid weights (from the project brief, not tuned on this test period): `{"collaborative": 0.6, "content": 0.3, "popularity": 0.1}`.


### Limitations

* Offline metrics on one split are noisy; confirm with an online A/B test before trusting small differences.
* Only *new*-product purchases count as hits, so absolute precision is low by design.
* Item similarities are pruned/cached per run; results are deterministic given `RANDOM_STATE` but depend on the evaluation sample size.
